hypotheses.reasoning: A payment-svc rolling deploy (v4.4.0) briefly drained an instance, which reduced capacity to 3/4. That small trigger would have been survivable alone. order-service retries payment-svc immediately, with up to 4 attempts, jitter off and backoff disabled. The retries pushed load to 3.2x expected (inflight=843), so payment-svc began load shedding with 503 (queue full). order-service then returned 503 and the gateway returned 503 on /checkout after retries were exhausted. The load stayed high after the instance came back (capacity 4/4) because of the retry storm, which is why it did not recover.
The onset coincides with the payment-svc v4.4.0 rollout. However, the logs show no errors from the new code itself.

verdict.recommendedAction: Re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget in order-service's PaymentClient. Temporarily lower retries, or shed load at order-service, so payment-svc can drain its queue. Verify that all payment-svc instances are healthy after the rollout. Add rollout capacity safeguards.
